name: Armistice Corridor

detectability.signature: Twin gravitational apertures connected by a faintly luminous spatial fold, emitting steady tachyon pulses

proximity: Sensor arrays detect mirrored readings from the opposite aperture
Mild gravitational shear causes cosmetic hull flexion
Navigation computers auto-flag the corridor as a valid transit route
contact: Instantaneous translocation across 4.7 light-years to the opposite aperture
Momentary sensory blackout for all biological crew during transit
Minor electromagnetic discharge across external hull plating
prolonged_exposure: Repeated transits cause cumulative neurological disorientation in organic beings
Ship chronometers develop persistent micro-drift after dozens of passages
Hull molecular bonds weaken subtly with each crossing, requiring periodic reinforcement

age: Estimated 800 years old based on surrounding spatial stress patterns
phenomena: A pale golden light fills the corridor interior, casting no shadows on transiting vessels
Sound-analogous vibrations propagate through the corridor walls at harmonic intervals
Objects placed at the exact midpoint of the corridor appear to exist at both endpoints simultaneously
Weapon systems experience a brief full-shutdown when entering either aperture
hazards: Vessels exceeding 600 meters in beam cannot fit through the apertures without structural damage
The weapon-dampening effect leaves transiting ships momentarily defenseless
Political disputes over corridor access have historically escalated to armed confrontation
opportunities: Provides a stable, reliable shortcut across 4.7 light-years of otherwise hazardous space
The weapon-dampening phenomenon is studied by pacifist researchers seeking to replicate it
Control of either aperture represents enormous strategic and commercial value
known_incidents: The Treaty of Keldane was signed at the corridor's midpoint in 3402, ending the Voss-Meridian Conflict, after delegates discovered they could not arm weapons inside the passage
A blockade of the northern aperture by the Ironmark Compact in 3471 triggered a three-month trade war before neutral arbitrators intervened
description: The Armistice Corridor is an artificial wormhole spanning 4.7 light-years, connecting two otherwise isolated star systems through a passage of folded space roughly 1,200 kilometers in diameter. Its twin apertures glow with a warm golden luminescence, and the interior of the corridor is suffused with a steady, shadowless light that crews describe as deeply calming. The structure is remarkably clean in its geometry, suggesting deliberate and sophisticated engineering.

Transit through the corridor is instantaneous and reliable, though biological crew experience a momentary sensory blackout during passage. Most notably, all weapon systems aboard transiting vessels undergo a complete shutdown upon entering either aperture, a phenomenon that persists until the ship exits the opposite end. This effect has proven impossible to circumvent despite centuries of military engineering efforts, and it has profoundly shaped the corridor's political significance.

The corridor's builders remain unknown, but the structure is estimated to be approximately eight centuries old. Its name derives from its most famous historical role: the Treaty of Keldane, negotiated at the corridor's exact midpoint where delegates from warring factions found themselves literally unable to threaten one another. Some scholars believe the corridor was built specifically as a demilitarized passage, a piece of infrastructure designed to enforce peace through physics.

Today the Armistice Corridor is one of the most heavily trafficked and politically contested transit points in the sector. Both aperture systems maintain permanent diplomatic stations, and access rights are governed by multilateral treaty. Researchers continue to study the weapon-dampening effect, hoping to understand the technology behind it. Meanwhile, smugglers and diplomats alike value the corridor for its unique guarantee: whatever else may happen, no shot can be fired inside.
